extracted.intended_audience: Applicants to and reviewers for DFG research funding (Germany); DFG review board members
extracted.subtask_description: Official DFG guidance listing the primary evaluation criteria, stage-wise review considerations, explicit non-scientific exclusions, and caveats for assessing applicant track records for research funding decisions in Germany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific quality of the proposed research
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three primary evaluation criteria: the scientific quality of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as the central criterion; at Stage 1 this is assessed by external reviewers via research question quality, methodological approach, and feasibility. Review boards contextualize individual reviews and compare scientific quality relative to the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of the project
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three primary evaluation criteria: the originality of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessed in terms of innovation and novelty. External reviewers explicitly evaluate innovation; review boards judge originality in disciplinary context when ranking proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to the field
rubrics_metrics.description: One of three primary evaluation criteria: the project's relevance to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated for whether the work addresses important questions or advances the discipline; considered alongside scientific quality and originality in final funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research question quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 criterion: reviewers evaluate the quality of the research question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess clarity, scientific significance, and whether the question is well-formulated and addressable within the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 criterion: reviewers evaluate the methodological approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment focuses on appropriateness, rigor, and suitability of methods to answer the research question; includes feasibility of planned methods and whether they are state-of-the-art or fit the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 criterion: reviewers evaluate the feasibility of the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes practicality of the timeline, resources, technical feasibility, and likelihood that the project can achieve stated objectives given the team and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 criterion: reviewers assess the qualifications of the applicant(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment takes into account track record, expertise, and capacity to carry out the project; see Track-record Assessment Caveat for how effective research time and publication selection should be handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 criterion: reviewers explicitly evaluate the innovation of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closely tied to originality; reviewers consider whether the project advances new concepts, methods, or directions and how it differentiates from existing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding in current literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 criterion: reviewers judge how well the proposal is embedded in the current literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators consider whether the proposal demonstrates awareness of relevant prior work, situates the research properly, and builds logically on the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of the reviews themselves
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 2 criterion: review board members judge the quality of individual external reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards assess whether reviews are thorough, well-justified, and informed; this influences how much weight is given to particular reviews during board discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of reviewer selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 2 criterion: review boards evaluate whether selected reviewers were appropriate for the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes checking for disciplinary fit, expertise, and potential conflicts; boards may downgrade or discount reviews if reviewer selection was inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative ranking within the discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 2 criterion: review boards place proposals in comparative ranking within the discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boards contextualize proposals relative to peer submissions in the discipline to inform funding priorities and relative merit judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 3 consideration: the Joint Committee considers strategic priorities when making final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final funding decisions may take broader strategic goals into account (e.g., portfolio balance, national research priorities) in addition to scientific assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 3 consideration: budget availability is considered by the Joint Committee in final decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even highly rated proposals may be limited by available funds; budget constraints inform which proposals can be supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 3 consideration: the Joint Committee assesses programmatic fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a proposal aligns with the specific aims, scope, and funding mechanisms of programs influences final selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit non-scientific criteria excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: DFG mandates that certain non-scientific criteria must NOT influence funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exclusion list includes: absolute age of the applicant; gender; ethnic origin; sexual orientation; illness or disability; family status / parental leave history; and career interruptions (these are explicitly accommodated rather than penalized). Reviewers must not consider these factors when evaluating proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track-record assessment caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on how to assess applicants' scientific output and track record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators should consider effective research time (excluding parental/medical leave, military service, etc.), prioritize quality (not quantity) of selected publications, and consider at most 10 publications per applicant when assessing track record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusionary anti-rubric principle
rubrics_metrics.description: DFG's model explicitly treats 'non-scientific criteria' as an anti-rubric to be excluded from review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle is highlighted as a design feature of DFG review guidance (noting it is comparatively rare in some other systems such as US/UK funders); rubrics should therefore explicitly state prohibited considerations rather than only listing what to consider.
